captions.instagram:
You tap the menu button. Nothing happens. You tap again.

We tested 12,621 Australian small-business websites in Google’s lab test on a simulated mid-range phone. 17.6% were too busy to answer a tap for more than 0.6 seconds in total while they loaded. Only 57.3% kept it to 0.2 seconds or less, which Google calls good.

The usual cause is code the visitor never asked for: chat widgets, trackers and heavy themes all starting at once.

captions.linkedin:
A page can look ready and still ignore your tap.

In our test of 12,621 Australian small-business websites (Google Lighthouse, simulated mid-range phone), 17.6% were too busy to respond to a tap for more than 0.6 seconds in total while loading. Google calls that poor. 57.3% kept it to 0.2 seconds or less, which Google calls good.

The page is not broken. It is busy running code in the background: chat and booking widgets, tracking scripts, theme effects. Each one queues up before the visitor’s tap gets a turn.

It is a lab test, one run per site, so it is a warning light rather than a verdict. But the fix is usually to load less, not to add more.
